Strategy & Investment Book Page 02 · Two Engines, One Investment
The Investment Thesis

Two engines.
One investment.

InPursuit operates two revenue engines that share a single technology and operational foundation. The bridge round funds the rails — one set of capital, two compounding revenue lines, both live by July 2026.

Engine 01 · Direct to Consumer
The InPursuit App.
A universal, all-payer consumer app on Apple App Store and Google Play. Four tiers — Free, Plus, Family, and Premium. Subscription revenue plus a Rokt-style commerce layer where brands bid on anonymized health signals and users earn cashback, HSA/FSA credits, or discounts.
Launches mid-July 2026 · D2C subscription
Engine 02 · Clinical Services Org
Multi-payer billing.
InPursuit becomes a Clinical Services Organization billing Medicare, Medicare Advantage, commercial, and Medicaid managed care directly under its own NPI. RPM, CCM, TCM, BHI today; ACCESS Model outcome-aligned payments layered on starting Cohort 2 in January 2027.
RPM live now · Multi-payer FFS + OAP upside
One Cap Table · One Investment
Both engines run on shared infrastructure and a single corporate entity. One round funds both. Revenue consolidates at InPursuit Health.
$2M bridge. Both engines to revenue.

Every dollar in this round builds shared rails — the integrations, the launch infrastructure, and the operational machinery that serve Engine 1 and Engine 2 simultaneously. There is no Engine 1 round and Engine 2 round. There is one round that lights both up.

01
Production launch infrastructure App Store and Google Play production. Medicare App Library certification. White House launch in market by mid-July 2026.
02
Universal payer integrations NPI billing operations. CMS Blue Button, CommonWell, eHealth Exchange, Surescripts. The connective tissue both engines bill against.
03
Clinical services build-out ACCESS Model billing operations. RPM, CCM, TCM, BHI workflows. Honeycomb deployment scaled across the panel.
04
Compliance & go-to-market HIPAA controls, federal compliance posture, and the targeted GTM motion that turns federal validation into recurring payer and consumer revenue.
The bridge is not a runway extension.   It is the capital that turns federal validation into two compounding revenue lines, both live by July 2026.

The Fragmentation Problem
Everyone has the data. No one can use it.
One EHR at the cardiologist. Another at the PCP. Pharmacy at CVS. Labs at Quest. Insurance at Aetna. Apple Watch on the wrist. Fitbit in the drawer. The fragmentation isn't a market feature — it's the unsolved problem itself. And it persists because the infrastructure layer doesn't exist in the consumer market.
Competitive Landscape · Point Solutions Without Infrastructure
Apple Health / Google Health
Device companions. Aggregate some wearable + limited clinical data.
Cannot orchestrate the full care continuum. No NPI, no payer billing, no commerce model.
Epic MyChart
Patient portal for Epic's 250+ health systems. Records from Epic-installed providers.
Cannot unify across EHR vendors. No wearables, no AI, no commerce.
GoodRx
Rx price comparison. $800M+ revenue solving one narrow problem exceptionally well.
Cannot unify records, integrate clinical data, or deliver intelligence beyond pricing.
Noom / Headspace / Calm
Content-first coaching. Noom reached $4B+ valuation on single-condition behavior change.
Cannot connect interventions to clinical outcomes, payer data, or care continuum.
The Pattern · And Our Thesis
Single-problem point solutions reach hundreds of millions in revenue. An infrastructure-powered consumer app that unifies the record, integrates wearables, delivers AI, surfaces savings, and adds a commerce layer isn't competing with any one of them. It's creating a new category.

Features, Pricing & Projections Page 10 · Pricing Strategy
Pricing Strategy Analysis

Are we underpriced?

Answer: probably yes — for what Plus actually delivers. But launch is not the time to find out. Aggressive Year 1 pricing drives adoption and conversion. Year 2+ gives us the data to optimize.

Plus ($14.99/mo) vs. equivalent single-purpose apps
If a user wants...They payTo get what Plus gives them
Contactless vitals (InPursuit Reflect) $9.99/mo + $100+ device Fitbit Premium requires a Fitbit
AI health coach $17–70/mo Noom blended ARPU
Nutrition tracking $19.99/mo MyFitnessPal Premium
Fitness content $12.99–24/mo Peloton App
Insurance optimization No consumer equivalent Enterprise tools only
InPursuit Plus$14.99/moAll of the above — plus the unified record
Should we charge more?

A user subscribing to Noom ($55) + Fitbit Premium ($10) + MyFitnessPal ($20) pays $85/month for overlapping single-purpose apps. InPursuit Plus delivers all three domains plus the unified record and insurance intelligence for $14.99. We could charge $24.99 and still be the bargain. We're not raising launch pricing — but this is the data that supports a Year 2 price test.

Why we're holding pricing at launch

Adoption compounds. At $14.99, Plus is below the psychological threshold where users deliberate — it's a "just try it" decision. The $15 price point is proven to maximize trial-to-paid conversion in health apps. Once we have 100,000+ Plus subscribers and 6 months of retention data, we have leverage to test a $19.99 tier, a "Plus Pro" at $24.99, or promotional bundles — without disrupting existing subscriber economics.

What Comes Next Page 13 · Engine 2 · Tee-Up
Engine 2 · Reimbursable Clinical Services · Modeled separately

This is where InPursuit becomes a healthcare company.

Engine 1 builds the audience. Engine 2 monetizes it through reimbursable clinical services billed under InPursuit's NPI. The same infrastructure stack — the same record, the same vitals, the same Goal Engine — powers four CMS-recognized service lines, each generating per-patient annual revenue measured in hundreds to low thousands. This document does not project Engine 2. It is the next deck.

RPM
Remote Patient Monitoring
CPT 99453, 99454, 99457. InPursuit Reflect™ + connected devices feed validated vitals to the care team. CMS reimburses ~$120/patient/month for active monitoring.
CCM
Chronic Care Management
CPT 99490, 99491, 99487. The unified record + Feed + AI guidance support 20+ minutes/month of non-face-to-face care for patients with 2+ chronic conditions. CMS reimburses ~$65–$120/patient/month.
TCM
Transitional Care Management
CPT 99495, 99496. Post-discharge coordination — exactly what every Plus subscriber's record + care team flow already enables. CMS reimburses ~$200–$280/patient per qualifying episode.
ACCESS
CMS ACCESS Model
Outcome-aligned payment program. Premium tier users have already declared their goals — perfectly aligned with outcome-based reimbursement. OAP rates: $180–$420 per patient per year per qualifying track. The Goal Engine becomes the qualifying mechanism.
The Thesis
Engine 1 is the funnel.
Engine 2 is the monetization.
Every Free user is a future RPM patient. Every Plus subscriber is a high-engagement TCM candidate after a hospital discharge. Every Premium user is already producing the data the ACCESS Model rewards. The infrastructure that makes the consumer app work is the same infrastructure that makes the clinical services bill — that is the entire moat. Engine 1 makes Engine 2 possible. Engine 2 makes Engine 1 worth building.

Engine 2b · ACCESS Model
Engine 2b · ACCESS Model

Outcome-aligned payments. The upside layer.

ACCESS is CMS's 10-year outcome-aligned payment model for technology-supported chronic care. Four clinical tracks. Fixed per-patient rates. Upside on top of the Engine 2a fee-for-service base. Cohort 2 go-live: January 2027.

How the Payment Works
Fixed per-patient-per-year rates paid monthly at half-cap for the first six months, with the balance withheld and reconciled at the twelve-month mark. Full release of the withhold depends on the Outcome Attainment Rate — the percentage of enrolled patients who hit the required clinical targets. The OAT threshold is 50% for the first 18 months, creating a ramp rather than a switch. ACCESS is genuine upside, but it is not a hockey stick.
ACCESS is the upside layer. Engine 2a is the revenue engine. Together they form a base plus additive architecture that holds up whether CMS tunes the ACCESS mechanics up or down over the 10-year performance period.

The ACCESS Model provides upside. The fourteen-payer pledge extends that upside across one hundred sixty-five million lives by 2028. The MSO-PC corporate structure enables clinical delivery in every state in America. And none of this requires the investor to fund a second company.

One cap table. One investment. Revenue flows to InPursuit Health, LLC from every payer, in every state, through every clinically eligible patient. The infrastructure is the moat.
